OpenAPI Integrations

The practical five-step flow for importing an OpenAPI spec, curating tool drafts, and publishing governed tools from it. Preview: off by default; enable with CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS.

System userDeveloperOperatorHow ToBETA
PrerequisitesA CALIBER deployment with admin or operator scope and CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true
Reviewed 2026-10-15 · current main branch docs contract

Disabled by default. OpenAPI integrations are a preview area and are off by default; enable with CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true and restart CALIBER (the same flag turns on MCP servers). While it is off, the /openapi-integrations* routes answer 404 (reason_code: feature_disabled) and the OpenAPI Integrations page is hidden. Tools already published from an integration stay in the tool registry. Enabling the flag means you accept preview behavior. See Feature flags.

Use this page when the practical question is how to bring a third-party OpenAPI spec into CALIBER, decide which operations should become agent-facing tools, and publish them safely.

At a glance#

TaskStart hereDeep reference

publish and use in a workflowpublish a ready draft, bind it like any toolWorkflows, Tools

1. The five-step flow#

  1. Create the integration shell — POST /openapi-integrations (or caliber.openapi_integrations.create(name)). This is just an identity; no spec exists yet.
  2. Import a version — paste JSON/YAML, upload a file, or supply a URL. A URL fetch goes through the same guarded egress every tool execution does, so an internal-only or blocked host is refused before any request is sent. Re-importing the identical document is rejected with a pointer to the existing version rather than silently duplicating it.
  3. Review operations and dependencies — every operation is classified (read/write/external_action, pagination style, async-job shape) and deterministic dependency detection runs automatically. High-confidence rows (an explicit OpenAPI link) are auto-wired; everything else is a suggestion or an advisory hint an operator can confirm or reject.
  4. Generate tool drafts — select operations by id, or by tags/methods/path_prefix filter for a large spec. Binding several related operations (list + get + create for one resource, say) into one tool pack keeps a curated spec from producing dozens of near-identical tools.
  5. Publish — a ready draft (server URL set, auth bound if the operation requires it, every secret reference resolvable) becomes a normal CaliberToolRegistry row. From that point it behaves exactly like a hand-registered tool: it shows up in the tool registry, can be bound into a workflow, and is reachable through client.tools.

Publishing is project-aware. The caller must have resource.publish in the selected project's effective permissions, which is granted to the project owner and editor roles, and the global caliber.operator scope. An organization-wide publish still requires the global admin scope. Creating an integration, importing a version, reviewing a dependency and generating or editing drafts need owner or editor in the project, and a preview needs reviewer, editor or owner; a member with too weak a role gets 403 and a person outside the project gets 404. A successful publish returns the published tool alongside the updated draft, so the UI/SDK can show what happened immediately rather than leaving the draft in an ambiguous state.

2. Common tasks#

You want to...Read this next
import from a URL instead of pastingArchitecture §4 — POST .../validate-spec-source checks reachability first
see what changed since the last importPOST .../reimport (url sources only), or POST .../versions/{id}/diff
bundle several operations behind one toolgenerate_tool_drafts(..., group_as_pack=True)
test a draft before publishingpreview_tool_draft() — refused unless allow_in_preview is set; in the reference profile it previews only a read operation (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS), see below
understand why a dependency is only advisoryArchitecture §7 — only deterministic rules auto-wire
call a published tool from an Aria sessionuse openapi_tool.list / openapi_tool.invoke for the stable bridge (invoke only runs read-only tools that do not need approval), or call the dynamically projected published tool directly (only read tools are projected). Only a tool whose operation reads (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) runs from Aria: a write is refused with unsupported_effect_path and nothing is sent (a write goes through a workflow tool node, which records an approvable proposal)

3. Common failure modes#

SymptomFirst thing to check
There is no OpenAPI Integrations page, or a call answers 404 with reason_code: feature_disabledCALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS is off (the default); set it to true and restart
Import from a URL fails immediatelythe host is blocked by egress policy (loopback, link-local, private range) — allowlist it if intentional
A draft won't publishits server URL is unset, or the operation requires auth and no binding is set, or a bound secret reference does not resolve
A draft is ready but publish is refusedcheck the selected project's access_role/permissions; owner or editor is required for project publication
preview returns 409the draft's allow_in_preview flag is off — set it explicitly, since preview performs a real upstream call
preview returns 409 with reason_code: unsupported_effect_paththe server runs the reference profile, where preview is read-only and your draft's operation is not a GET, HEAD or OPTIONS. Nothing was sent. Publish the tool and call it from a workflow tool node, which records an approvable proposal; see Draft preview is read-only
A dependency never shows up as canonicalit was a low-confidence, same-tag-only signal — advisory hints require operator confirmation, they never auto-wire
A published tool is refused in a workflow: OpenAPI effect proposal refused: <code>the call is protected (any method but GET, HEAD or OPTIONS, or a tool published as write or external_action) and failed a check before an approval was requested: openapi_egress_blocked (the server or OAuth token URL is not allowed by the egress policy), openapi_input_invalid (the input breaks the tool's schema), openapi_key_override_refused (do not send an idempotency key: the platform sends its own), openapi_precondition_conflict (expected_resource_version and the If-Match header disagree). Nothing was sent. See Governed OpenAPI tools
A published write tool is unknown after the downstream timed outthe request left and the answer never came, so CALIBER does not resend it: settle it with the receipt verifier, a receipt callback or an operator, not by running the node again
A tool works from a workflow but not from Ariacheck whether it is approval-gated or whether the current Aria mode hides its side-effect tier. A read tool that does not need approval is projected in every mode. A write / external_action tool is not projected in any mode (the public executor refuses a protected method, so the call could only fail). A tool that requires approval is never projected as a direct Aria tool. A tool published as read whose operation is a POST is projected but answers unsupported_effect_path when called (the public executor refuses a protected method)
